<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as peppers

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers peppers in 3 forms kept separate in every comparison: peppers, as sold (684 results), peppers, powder or ground (111 results) and peppers, dried (34 results).<sup <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-peppers" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-peppers-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of peppers, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤30</td><td>≤30</td><td>30–4140 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤30</td><td>≤30</td><td>30–4140 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>189 reference units; 3 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>185</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Ericson et al. 2020</td><td>3</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Stojanović et al. 2021</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for peppers, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead" class="internal" data-slug="sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead" data-no-cite-meta>Ericson et al. 2020</a></li><li><a href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Stojanović et al. 2021</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach peppers

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach peppers comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Peppers, as sold from Location B1 (industrial-affected area) had total mercury higher at 62.1 µg/kg, against 0.93 µg/kg for Control (grocery store >55 km from any power plant) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, peppers, as sold from harvest C4 (mining-affected area) had total mercury higher at 0.4 µg/kg, against 0.1 µg/kg for harvest C1 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/duranteyanez2026-colombia-sweet-pepper-mining-soils|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Durante-Yánez EV, Urango-Cárdenas ID, Enamorado-Montes GH, Laza-Durante M, Combatt Caballero E, Marrugo-Negrete J, Paternina-Uribe R, Díez S · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/duranteyanez2026-colombia-sweet-pepper-mining-soils">Metal uptake in sweet peppers cultivated in soils contaminated by artisanal gold mining: implications for food safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health (2026) 48:223</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/duranteyanez2026-colombia-sweet-pepper-mining-soils">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that peppers, powder or ground from laboratory-prepared control had total arsenic higher at 21,800 µg/kg, against 17,100 µg/kg for all seven samples in Table 2, including the laboratory control in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Awoyale W, Zorbari NL, Sanni LO · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals">Aflatoxin content and heavy metals composition of powdered pepper from selected markets in Kwara state, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Preservation 2024, 31(5): 811-817</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>

regions, with subgroup medians from 0.04 to 6,740 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-peppers" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-peppers" data-question="How do heavy metals get into peppers?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into peppers?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, peppers from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than peppers from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Awoyale W, Zorbari NL, Sanni LO · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals">Aflatoxin content and heavy metals composition of powdered pepper from selected markets in Kwara state, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Preservation 2024, 31(5): 811-817</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Peppers, powder or ground from laboratory-prepared control had total arsenic higher at 21,800 µg/kg, against 17,100 µg/kg for all seven samples in Table 2, including the laboratory control in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Awoyale W, Zorbari NL, Sanni LO · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals">Aflatoxin content and heavy metals composition of powdered pepper from selected markets in Kwara state, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Preservation 2024, 31(5): 811-817</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/awoyale2024-kwara-powdered-pepper-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-peppers-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-peppers-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of peppers have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of peppers have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, the HMI reference median was lowest for peppers, as sold (25 µg/kg) and highest for peppers, dried (154 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-peppers" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-peppers" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in peppers?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in peppers?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, peppers, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in SEARO (0.04 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (6,740 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in AFRO (4 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (108 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-peppers" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-peppers" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in peppers?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in peppers?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same peppers.<sup class="cite">[[sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Stojanović B, Janković S, Đorđević V, Marjanović S, Vasilev D, Stojanović Z, Balaban M, Antić V · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals">Determination of toxic elements in meat products from Serbia packaged in tinplate cans</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Research Square preprint, posted 26 February 2021 (version 1)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Peppers, powder or ground (ingredient for canned meatballs in tomato sauce) had lead lower at 20 µg/kg, against 30 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (peppers, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Stojanović B, Janković S, Đorđević V, Marjanović S, Vasilev D, Stojanović Z, Balaban M, Antić V · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals">Determination of toxic elements in meat products from Serbia packaged in tinplate cans</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Research Square preprint, posted 26 February 2021 (version 1)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-peppers-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-peppers-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in peppers is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in peppers is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 15 results from 4 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D, Devesa V, Font G, Yusà V · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Assessment of metal levels in foodstuffs from the Region of Valencia (Spain)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 654-670</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|23]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 69.9 µg/kg (mean) in peppers, as sold from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>
